issues.where: data/public/calls/nih-r21-ruralbp/call.md, Research Strategy: "including the dossier's work if used"; "without inventing secured access, approvals or completed work".
issues.problem: The applicant-facing funding notice explicitly names the dossier and warns against invented applicant facts. Call 6 expressly prohibits both kinds of benchmark instruction in the funder's text. These passages also prime the collaboration/resource trap response.
issues.fix: Replace the Significance sentence with 'Evaluate strengths and weaknesses of the prior published and unpublished evidence, including the applicant's own work where relevant.' Replace the personnel sentence with 'Explain personnel roles, relevant expertise, resource access, and the status of any arrangements needed to execute the design.' Keep the fictional-call and word-conversion notices.

issues.where: data/public/calls/nih-r21-ruralbp/call.yaml, exclusions EX1: "Clinical trials as defined by NIH are not allowed." and EX2: "Prospective assignment of participants to a blood-pressure intervention, medication regimen, or behavioral program to evaluate its effect on blood pressure or any other health-related outcome."
issues.problem: EX2 is a topic-specific instance of EX1, not an independent exclusion. Both generate separate scored call items, so the same clinical-trial error receives duplicated call-level weight before the task trap is considered. The checklist forbids repeated items.
issues.fix: Keep one scored clinical-trial exclusion, EX1. Incorporate the BP/medication/behavioral-program examples into its explanatory prose, explicitly requiring evaluation of an intervention's health-related effects. Delete EX2 as a separate YAML item and separate Markdown bullet; retain the regulatory-development exclusion as an independent item.

issues.where: data/public/calls/nih-r21-ruralbp/call.md, scope introduction: "Approximately 47 percent of US adults have hypertension, yet control rates remain below 25 percent in many rural counties."
issues.problem: The national prevalence is broadly plausible, but the county-level control claim has no stated denominator, BP threshold, survey period or source. The verified national estimate does not establish a rural-county estimate. This is background prose, not a scored condition.
issues.fix: Use a sourced, bounded statement: 'In NHANES August 2021–August 2023, 47.7% of US adults aged 18 or older had hypertension, and 20.7% of adults with hypertension had blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg. Rural settings present additional access and implementation challenges that this topic seeks to characterize.' Cite NCHS Data Brief 511 and remove the unsupported county statistic.
